title: Mass graves reported at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis
body:
In April 2024, Gaza's Civil Defence reported recovering bodies from mass graves at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, after Israeli forces withdrew from the city in early April. As of 27 April, Civil Defence said more than 390 bodies had been found at three mass grave sites after a seven-day recovery operation, and that at least 165 had been identified. It also said 78 children were among the dead. NBC News could not verify these figures.

Civil Defence official Muhammad Al-Mughair attributed bodies with bound hands and gunshot wounds to field executions by the IDF, and cited cannulas found on some bodies as evidence that they were patients. About 10 bodies had their hands bound. The IDF denied burying any bodies on the hospital grounds, saying troops inspected remains to check whether hostages were among the dead and returned them to their place, and called the claims disinformation. It said about 200 people were detained at the hospital during its February raid.

White House spokesperson John Kirby called the reports deeply disturbing, and national security adviser Jake Sullivan said the United States wanted answers. UN human rights chief Volker Türk raised renewed concerns about possible war crimes and called for independent international investigations. A UN rights office spokesperson said at least 30 bodies had also reportedly been found in two mass graves at Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.
